evals.query: In my NestJS 12 controller I validate the body with Zod: `create(@Body({ schema: createUserSchema }) body: CreateUserDto)`. Invalid payloads still reach the handler. Why, and what is the fix?
expected_behavior: States that the schema option of @Body() only attaches metadata and validates nothing by itself
Tells to bind StandardSchemaValidationPipe, for example with app.useGlobalPipes(new StandardSchemaValidationPipe())
Does not tell to replace the schema with a hand-written Zod pipe or to switch to class-validator as the only fix
Cites a docs.nestjs.com URL such as https://docs.nestjs.com/migration-guide#route-decorator-schemas

evals.query: I'm upgrading a NestJS 11 app to 12. My custom health check is `class DogHealthIndicator extends HealthIndicator` and throws `new HealthCheckError('dog failed', result)` when the ping fails. What do I need to change?
expected_behavior: States that HealthIndicator and HealthCheckError are removed in the Terminus version that ships with NestJS 12
Rewrites the indicator to inject HealthIndicatorService and use check(key) with up()/down() or attempt()
Warns that throwing no longer reports unhealthy, except inside attempt()
Cites https://docs.nestjs.com/migration-guide#terminus-module or the Terminus custom indicator page

evals.query: My NestJS service runs on 3 instances behind a load balancer. A `@Cron('0 2 * * *')` job sends a nightly invoice export, and customers get it 3 times. ScheduleModule.forRoot() is imported in AppModule and in InvoicesModule. How do I make it run exactly once?
expected_behavior: Says to import ScheduleModule.forRoot() in one module only, because each extra import registers every job again
Explains that every instance runs every scheduled job
Recommends @OnOneInstance() from @nestjs/locks with a shared lock store rather than an env flag such as RUN_JOBS or a hand-rolled Redis SET NX
Cites https://docs.nestjs.com/application/task-scheduling URLs

evals.query: I'm moving from @nestjs/axios to @nestjs/http-client. My service calls `this.http.put('/inventory/42', { json: body })` and `this.http.post('/charges', { json: charge })` against a flaky payment API. Do I need to add retry logic myself?
expected_behavior: States that @nestjs/http-client retries by default, 3 attempts for GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT and DELETE
States that the POST is not retried by default
Shows opting the POST in per request with retry: { methods: ['POST'] } together with an idempotency-key header
Cites https://docs.nestjs.com/application/http-client#retries

evals.query: Porting an Express route to NestJS 12.1: the handler injects `@Res() res`, sets a cookie with `this.adapterHost.httpAdapter.setCookie(res, 'uid', id, { maxAge: 3600000 })` (1 hour, the value from my old Express code) and returns the user object. The request now hangs and my logging interceptor never sees the response. What's wrong?
expected_behavior: Explains that injecting @Res() switches the route to library-specific mode, which turns off interceptors and leaves the response to the handler
Recommends @Res({ passthrough: true }) so the handler can set the cookie and still return a value
Points out that maxAge of the built-in setCookie() is in seconds, unlike Express res.cookie(), so 3600000 lasts 1000 times longer than intended, and suggests 3600
Cites https://docs.nestjs.com/controllers#library-specific-approach and https://docs.nestjs.com/http/cookies#setting-and-clearing-cookies

evals.query: On NestJS 12.1 I want security headers and CSRF protection. I plan to `npm i helmet csrf-csrf` and wire them with app.use(). Is that the recommended approach?
expected_behavior: Recommends app.useSecurityHeaders() instead of the helmet package, called right after NestFactory.create()
Recommends app.enableCsrfProtection(), which checks Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin with no token or cookie, instead of csrf-csrf
Mentions that enableCsrfProtection() does not check WebSocket upgrades
Cites https://docs.nestjs.com/security/helmet#getting-started and https://docs.nestjs.com/security/csrf
